C1.name: SWAPI solar wind and pickup-ion instrument on IMAP
C1.evidence: Designed, built and calibrated in the Princeton Space Physics Lab; IMAP launched Sep 24, 2025 and SWAPI is operating.

C2.name: Princeton-led IMAP mission
C2.evidence: Princeton leads IMAP; APL builds and operates the spacecraft.

C3.name: Energetic particle, ENA and polar solar-wind missions
C3.evidence: PSP IS☉IS, IBEX, Ulysses/SWOOPS. Public record; please verify the wording.

C4.name: Ion and neutral beamline test and calibration facility
C4.evidence: Electron-impact ion source from about 100 eV to 30 keV, stable to within 10% over a day. A Wien filter selects H⁺, D⁺, He⁺, N₂⁺, Ne⁺, Ar⁺ and water-group ions, and a charge-exchange vessel with a precision nitrogen leak makes neutral beams. The 16 ft beamline expands the beam to about 60 mm, with 1, 3, 6 and 14 mm collimators and a Helmholtz coil that cancels Earth's field or dumps ions. Calibrated IMAP/SWAPI and IMAP-Lo, and cross-calibrated SWAPI with CoDICE.

C5.name: Cleanroom and vacuum chambers
C5.evidence: The 4 ft Main Chamber and the Science Chamber run at about 10⁻⁸–10⁻⁹ torr, watched by residual gas analyzers, and open into an ISO 7 (Class 10,000) cleanroom. Used for SWAPI flight-hardware assembly and test.

C6.name: Beam monitors and characterization: MCP, absolute beam monitors, CEM, Faraday cup with RPA
C6.evidence: On the beamline: an MCP, a carbon-foil and a conversion-surface absolute beam monitor (ABM), a channel electron multiplier (CEM), and a Faraday cup with retarding-potential (RPA) capability up to 5 kV. A dedicated RPA for beam energy and resolution is in design, and ABM and MCP characterization is set for the SWAPI EM+ calibration.

source.label: PSPL calibration system page; Mitchell's notes (Oct 2026)

C7.name: SWAPI EM+ engineering unit

C10.name: Dust impacts detected by electric-field instruments
C10.evidence: PSP, Solar Orbiter, Juno/Waves, MAVEN/LPW; active SolO GI (2024–2028) and NFDAP (2023–2027) awards.

C11.name: Dust-impact charge yield of PSP heat-shield (TPS) material
C11.evidence: Measurements in hand; JGR paper in preparation.

C12.name: SPICE-based orbit and geometry viewer (Ouimap Viewer)

C14.name: Calibration control system and data logging
C14.evidence: Valve states, pressures, cryopump temperatures, turbo-pump speeds and positioner locations are logged at about 1 Hz to a local database and shared with instrument teams.
